    LED control voltage vs sample intensity¶

    How much light reaches the sample for a given LED control voltage, on each scope and for each LED colour? A light meter at the sample plane reads the light while the control voltage is stepped. A straight line per LED then converts control voltage into photon flux density (PFD, µmol/m²/s). The acquisition script stores that line on the scope, for later experiments.

    Analysis written by Claude (Anthropic); conceptualised and verified by Yatharth Bhasin.

    Protocol¶

    Acquisition: single_channel_calibration() in scripts/calibration/control_volt_vs_sample_intensity.py.

    • Light meter: lux1, a TSL2561 on a Seeed Grove Digital Light Sensor, read by its own Pico at 16× gain and 101 ms. It sits on a 4.5 mm centring plate in the sample holder, about 5 mm above the sample-holder plane, and is moved from scope to scope.
    • Sweep: one LED colour at a time, from 0 to 2.9 V in 0.1 V steps, first with the beacon off and then on. Each point waits 0.2 s, then takes one reading.
    • Repeats: since trappyscopes 21b83ff each sweep runs four times (up, down, up, down), about 16 min per scope. Earlier runs swept up once per beacon state.
    • PWM: the LED driver is PWM at 3 MHz, which gives 42 duty levels, so the light changes in steps of 3.3/42 V whatever voltage is asked for.

    Data¶

    Runs are read with trappy-explorer's legacy reader, explorer.legacy.ExpExplorer. Each run has one stream per LED colour (red, green, blue), one row per reading. Each run also records what the light meter reported about itself (devices/lightmeter/config), and the fit the script stored on the scope (devices/<colour>/params).

    In [4]:
    Copied! 
    rich.get_console().quiet = True                           # the loader prints one line per run
exps = ExpExplorer.create_superset(DATA, extended_parse=True)
rich.get_console().quiet = False
print(exps)

ms = exps.df_events.query("type == 'measurement_stream'")
res = exps.df.assign(stream=exps.df.measureid.map(dict(zip(ms.measureid, ms.name))))
meta = {eid: d["metadata"] for eid, d in exps.data.items()}

def sensor_of(m):
    return (m.get("devices", {}).get("lightmeter") or {}).get("config") or {}

runs = pd.DataFrame([{"scope": m["name"].split("__")[0], "eid": eid, "started": m["created"],
                      **{k: sensor_of(m).get(k) for k in ("board", "chip", "gain", "integration_ms")}}
                     for eid, m in meta.items()]).set_index("scope").sort_index()
runs = runs.join(res.groupby(["eid", "stream"]).size().unstack(fill_value=0), on="eid")

    Sweep labels for runs recorded before 17 Nov 2026¶

    Until trappyscopes 3252c69, the script swept each colour once with the beacon off and once with it on, both upwards, and recorded no sweep or direction. For those runs the two sweeps are numbered here in the order they were taken. In a later run, missing labels stop the notebook instead.

    In [6]:
    Copied! 
    FIX = pd.Timestamp("2026-11-17")                          # trappyscopes 3252c69 / 21b83ff
before_fix = lambda scope: pd.Timestamp(runs.loc[scope, "started"]) < FIX
scope_of = runs.reset_index().set_index("eid").scope

d = res.assign(scope=res.eid.map(scope_of), channel=res.stream, t=pd.to_datetime(res.dt),
               V=res.volts.apply(lambda v: float(v[0]) if isinstance(v, (list, tuple)) else float(v)),
               counts=res.counts.astype(float), ch1=res.ch1.astype(float),
               beacon=res.beacon.astype(bool), saturated=res.saturated.astype(bool))
for s in d.scope.unique():
    rows = d.scope == s
    if "sweep" in d and d.loc[rows, "sweep"].notna().all():
        continue
    assert before_fix(s), f"{s}: no sweep labels in a run recorded after the fix"
    d.loc[rows, "sweep"] = d.loc[rows, "beacon"].astype(int)
    d.loc[rows, "direction"] = "up"
d["sweep"] = d.sweep.astype(int)
d = d[["scope", "eid", "channel", "V", "beacon", "sweep", "direction", "counts", "ch1", "saturated", "temp", "t"]]
d.groupby(["scope", "beacon", "sweep", "direction"]).size().unstack(["beacon", "sweep", "direction"])
    FIX = pd.Timestamp("2026-11-17") # trappyscopes 3252c69 / 21b83ff before_fix = lambda scope: pd.Timestamp(runs.loc[scope, "started"]) < FIX scope_of = runs.reset_index().set_index("eid").scope d = res.assign(scope=res.eid.map(scope_of), channel=res.stream, t=pd.to_datetime(res.dt), V=res.volts.apply(lambda v: float(v[0]) if isinstance(v, (list, tuple)) else float(v)), counts=res.counts.astype(float), ch1=res.ch1.astype(float), beacon=res.beacon.astype(bool), saturated=res.saturated.astype(bool)) for s in d.scope.unique(): rows = d.scope == s if "sweep" in d and d.loc[rows, "sweep"].notna().all(): continue assert before_fix(s), f"{s}: no sweep labels in a run recorded after the fix" d.loc[rows, "sweep"] = d.loc[rows, "beacon"].astype(int) d.loc[rows, "direction"] = "up" d["sweep"] = d.sweep.astype(int) d = d[["scope", "eid", "channel", "V", "beacon", "sweep", "direction", "counts", "ch1", "saturated", "temp", "t"]] d.groupby(["scope", "beacon", "sweep", "direction"]).size().unstack(["beacon", "sweep", "direction"])

    The light meter¶

    The conversion constants hold only for the chip, gain and integration time they were measured for. They come from the TAOS TSL2560/TSL2561 datasheet (TAOS059N, March 2009), TSL2561T/FN/CL column:

    • Re_640nm: ch0 counts per µW/cm² at 640 nm, 16× gain, 101 ms (typical). The same table allows 750–1250 counts for a nominal 1000, so the absolute scale is good to ±25% between chips. Scope-to-scope comparisons do not depend on it, because one sensor measures every scope.
    • colour_factors: ch0 responsivity at each LED's peak wavelength relative to 640 nm, read off Figure 4.

    Each run's sensor report must match.

    In [7]:
    Copied! 
    SENSOR = {"chip": "TSL2561T/FN/CL", "gain": 16, "integration_ms": 101,
          "Re_640nm": 27.5, "colour_factors": {"red": 1.00, "green": 0.91, "blue": 0.81},
          "full_scale": 37177}
check = runs[["board", "chip", "gain", "integration_ms"]].assign(
    matches=lambda r: (r.chip == SENSOR["chip"]) & (r.gain == SENSOR["gain"])
                      & (r.integration_ms == SENSOR["integration_ms"]))
assert check.matches.all(), "a run's light meter does not match the constants"
check
    SENSOR = {"chip": "TSL2561T/FN/CL", "gain": 16, "integration_ms": 101, "Re_640nm": 27.5, "colour_factors": {"red": 1.00, "green": 0.91, "blue": 0.81}, "full_scale": 37177} check = runs[["board", "chip", "gain", "integration_ms"]].assign( matches=lambda r: (r.chip == SENSOR["chip"]) & (r.gain == SENSOR["gain"]) & (r.integration_ms == SENSOR["integration_ms"])) assert check.matches.all(), "a run's light meter does not match the constants" check

    Which LED each channel lights¶

    The sensor's second photodiode (ch1) sees mostly near-infrared, so the ratio ch1/ch0 depends on the wavelength: highest for red, low for green, lowest for blue. Each point is one channel on one scope, at 1 V and above. A channel whose ratio sits with another colour lights that colour's LED. From here on each channel is analysed as the colour it actually lights; the table lists any that differ from their name.

    In [8]:
    Copied! 
    r = d[d.V >= 1].assign(ratio=lambda x: x.ch1 / x.counts).groupby(["scope", "channel"]).ratio.median()
measured = r.apply(lambda v: "red" if v > 0.1 else ("green" if v > 0.025 else "blue")).rename("colour")
d = d.join(measured, on=["scope", "channel"])

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 3.5))
for ch, g in r.rename("ratio").reset_index().groupby("channel"):
    g = g.set_index("scope").reindex(SCOPES)
    ax.plot(SCOPES, g.ratio, "o", color=LED[ch], label=f"named {ch}")
ax.set_ylabel("ch1 / ch0"); ax.set_yscale("log"); ax.legend()
plt.show()
measured.reset_index().query("channel != colour")
    r = d[d.V >= 1].assign(ratio=lambda x: x.ch1 / x.counts).groupby(["scope", "channel"]).ratio.median() measured = r.apply(lambda v: "red" if v > 0.1 else ("green" if v > 0.025 else "blue")).rename("colour") d = d.join(measured, on=["scope", "channel"]) fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 3.5)) for ch, g in r.rename("ratio").reset_index().groupby("channel"): g = g.set_index("scope").reindex(SCOPES) ax.plot(SCOPES, g.ratio, "o", color=LED[ch], label=f"named {ch}") ax.set_ylabel("ch1 / ch0"); ax.set_yscale("log"); ax.legend() plt.show() measured.reset_index().query("channel != colour")

    PWM levels¶

    The control voltage sets a PWM duty cycle. At 3 MHz on the Pico's 125 MHz clock there are 42 levels, and MicroPython 1.25 rounds each requested duty to the nearest one. The plot shows the voltage asked for against the voltage the PWM actually produces: equal steps would lie on a straight staircase; uneven steps are where two 0.1 V requests land one level apart or two. The fits below use the produced voltage.

    In [9]:
    Copied! 
    PWM_LEVELS, VREF = 42, 3.3
duty = 65535 - (d.V / VREF * 65535).astype(int)           # pwm_ca_channel.setV (common anode)
d["level"] = PWM_LEVELS - (duty * PWM_LEVELS + 65535 // 2) // 65535
d["V_pwm"] = d.level * VREF / PWM_LEVELS
produced = lambda V: (PWM_LEVELS - ((65535 - int(V / VREF * 65535)) * PWM_LEVELS + 65535 // 2)
                      // 65535) * VREF / PWM_LEVELS    # the same, for one requested voltage

v = d[["V", "V_pwm"]].drop_duplicates().sort_values("V")
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 4))
ax.step(v.V, v.V_pwm, where="mid", color="#0b0b0b")
ax.set_xlabel("control voltage asked for (V)"); ax.set_ylabel("voltage the PWM produces (V)")
plt.show()
    PWM_LEVELS, VREF = 42, 3.3 duty = 65535 - (d.V / VREF * 65535).astype(int) # pwm_ca_channel.setV (common anode) d["level"] = PWM_LEVELS - (duty * PWM_LEVELS + 65535 // 2) // 65535 d["V_pwm"] = d.level * VREF / PWM_LEVELS produced = lambda V: (PWM_LEVELS - ((65535 - int(V / VREF * 65535)) * PWM_LEVELS + 65535 // 2) // 65535) * VREF / PWM_LEVELS # the same, for one requested voltage v = d[["V", "V_pwm"]].drop_duplicates().sort_values("V") fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 4)) ax.step(v.V, v.V_pwm, where="mid", color="#0b0b0b") ax.set_xlabel("control voltage asked for (V)"); ax.set_ylabel("voltage the PWM produces (V)") plt.show()

    Raw readings¶

    Sensor counts (ch0) against the control voltage, every reading, one panel per scope, coloured by the LED each channel actually lights. Readings that sit on top of each other were repeatable. The flat start is the LED below its threshold; the small steps along each line are the PWM levels.

    In [10]:
    Copied! 
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 4, figsize=(13, 6), sharex=True, sharey=True)
for ax, s in zip(axes.flat, SCOPES):
    for colour, g in d[d.scope == s].groupby("colour"):
        ax.plot(g.V, g.counts, ".", ms=3, color=LED[colour], label=colour)
    ax.set_title(s)
for ax in axes[-1]:
    ax.set_xlabel("control voltage (V)")
for ax in axes[:, 0]:
    ax.set_ylabel("counts, ch0")
axes[0, -1].legend()
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 4, figsize=(13, 6), sharex=True, sharey=True) for ax, s in zip(axes.flat, SCOPES): for colour, g in d[d.scope == s].groupby("colour"): ax.plot(g.V, g.counts, ".", ms=3, color=LED[colour], label=colour) ax.set_title(s) for ax in axes[-1]: ax.set_xlabel("control voltage (V)") for ax in axes[:, 0]: ax.set_ylabel("counts, ch0") axes[0, -1].legend() plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

    Photon flux density¶

    ch0 counts give the irradiance at the sensor, E = counts / (Re_640nm × colour factor) µW/cm². For a narrow-band LED the photon flux density is PFD = E[W/m²] × λ[nm] / 119.6 µmol/m²/s, with λ each scope's own lambda_nm for that colour. Readings at the sensor's full-scale count are the ceiling, not the light, and are left out of the fits; the table counts them.

    In [11]:
    Copied! 
    lam = {(scope_of[eid], c): m["devices"][c]["params"]["lambda_nm"]
       for eid, m in meta.items() for c in ("red", "green", "blue")}
re = lambda colour: SENSOR["Re_640nm"] * SENSOR["colour_factors"][colour]
d["pfd"] = [c / re(k) * 0.01 * lam[(s, k)] / 119.6 for c, k, s in zip(d.counts, d.colour, d.scope)]
d.groupby(["scope", "colour"]).saturated.sum().unstack().reindex(SCOPES)
    lam = {(scope_of[eid], c): m["devices"][c]["params"]["lambda_nm"] for eid, m in meta.items() for c in ("red", "green", "blue")} re = lambda colour: SENSOR["Re_640nm"] * SENSOR["colour_factors"][colour] d["pfd"] = [c / re(k) * 0.01 * lam[(s, k)] / 119.6 for c, k, s in zip(d.counts, d.colour, d.scope)] d.groupby(["scope", "colour"]).saturated.sum().unstack().reindex(SCOPES)

    Fit¶

    One straight line per scope and colour, PFD = slope × V + intercept, against the produced voltage, over all readings from level 3 (about 0.2 V) up; below that the LED gives no light. resid_sd_pct is the scatter about the line as % of the PFD at full scale. The lack-of-fit test compares how far the readings at each level sit from the line with how far they sit from each other: lof_p below 0.05 means the line misses by more than the readings scatter, i.e. the response is not quite straight.

    In [12]:
    Copied! 
    fitted = d[(d.level >= 3) & ~d.saturated]

def fit(g):
    (m, c), cov = np.polyfit(g.V_pwm, g.pfd, 1, cov=True)
    res = g.pfd - (m * g.V_pwm + c)
    ss_res, top = (res ** 2).sum(), m * g.V_pwm.max() + c
    ss_pe = g.groupby("level").pfd.apply(lambda y: ((y - y.mean()) ** 2).sum()).sum()
    L, N = g.level.nunique(), len(g)
    F = ((ss_res - ss_pe) / (L - 2)) / (ss_pe / (N - L))
    return pd.Series({"slope": m, "intercept": c, "slope_se": np.sqrt(cov[0, 0]),
                      "r2": 1 - ss_res / ((g.pfd - g.pfd.mean()) ** 2).sum(),
                      "resid_sd_pct": 100 * np.sqrt(ss_res / (N - 2)) / top,
                      "readings_per_level": N / L, "lof_p": stats.f.sf(F, L - 2, N - L)})

fits = fitted.groupby(["scope", "colour"]).apply(fit, include_groups=False)
fits.round(4)
    fitted = d[(d.level >= 3) & ~d.saturated] def fit(g): (m, c), cov = np.polyfit(g.V_pwm, g.pfd, 1, cov=True) res = g.pfd - (m * g.V_pwm + c) ss_res, top = (res ** 2).sum(), m * g.V_pwm.max() + c ss_pe = g.groupby("level").pfd.apply(lambda y: ((y - y.mean()) ** 2).sum()).sum() L, N = g.level.nunique(), len(g) F = ((ss_res - ss_pe) / (L - 2)) / (ss_pe / (N - L)) return pd.Series({"slope": m, "intercept": c, "slope_se": np.sqrt(cov[0, 0]), "r2": 1 - ss_res / ((g.pfd - g.pfd.mean()) ** 2).sum(), "resid_sd_pct": 100 * np.sqrt(ss_res / (N - 2)) / top, "readings_per_level": N / L, "lof_p": stats.f.sf(F, L - 2, N - L)}) fits = fitted.groupby(["scope", "colour"]).apply(fit, include_groups=False) fits.round(4)

    Hysteresis¶

    At each level, the mean of the readings taken on the way up minus those taken on the way down, as % of the PFD at full scale. Zero means the light does not depend on the direction of approach. A consistent sign means the LED (or the light meter) lags: on the way up readings come out low if the light has not settled, on the way down high. Runs without a downward sweep cannot show this.

    In [15]:
    Copied! 
    has_down = d.groupby("scope").direction.apply(lambda x: (x == "down").any())

    h = fitted[fitted.scope.isin(has_down[has_down].index)]
    h = h.pivot_table(index=["scope", "colour", "V_pwm"], columns="direction", values="pfd")
    full = fits.slope * 2.9 + fits.intercept
    h["hyst_pct"] = 100 * (h["up"] - h["down"]) / full.reindex(h.index.droplevel("V_pwm")).to_numpy()
    hyst = h.hyst_pct.reset_index()

    Repeatability and the beacon¶

    repeat_pct: the spread of all readings at the same level (std / mean), median over levels from 1 V up, where one count is below 0.1% of the reading.

    beacon_pct: how much higher readings are with the beacon on than off, median over the same levels. The beacon-on sweeps always come after the beacon-off sweeps, so this also contains any drift between them. beacon_dark_counts separates the two: it is the beacon's own light, read with the LED off (levels 0 and 1), beacon on minus off. Near zero means the beacon adds no light at the sample, and any beacon_pct is drift.

    In [16]:
    Copied! 
    hi = fitted[fitted.V_pwm >= 1]
repeat = hi.groupby(["scope", "colour", "level"]).pfd.agg(lambda y: 100 * y.std() / y.mean())
repeat = repeat.groupby(["scope", "colour"]).median().rename("repeat_pct")
b = hi.pivot_table(index=["scope", "colour", "level"], columns="beacon", values="pfd")
beacon = (100 * (b[True] / b[False] - 1)).groupby(["scope", "colour"]).median().rename("beacon_pct")
dark = d[d.level <= 1].groupby(["scope", "beacon"]).counts.mean().unstack()
beacon_dark = (dark[True] - dark[False]).rename("beacon_dark_counts")
tab = pd.concat([repeat, beacon], axis=1).unstack("colour").reindex(SCOPES)
tab[("beacon_dark_counts", "")] = beacon_dark.reindex(SCOPES)
tab.round(3)

    Fleet¶

    Each scope's slope (PFD per volt) for each colour. Scopes on a horizontal line deliver the same light for the same control voltage; distance from the others is how much a scope needs its own calibration.

    What the script stored on the scope¶

    The script fits its own line when the run ends and stores it on the scope, one per channel. It fits against the voltage asked for, over every reading including the dead zone. This table compares the stored line's prediction with this notebook's fit at 1 V and 2 V asked for. The light at a requested voltage is that of the PWM level it lands on, so a line fitted against the requested voltage is off by up to half a step there.

    Green and blue convert to PFD almost identically with this sensor (λ divided by the colour factor is about 577 for both). So a channel that lights the other of those two colours still stores a line that is right for the light it delivers; only its colour is wrong.

    fleet = (fits.join(hyst_tab).join(repeat).join(beacon).reset_index() .merge(shelf.reset_index()[["scope", "channel", "colour", "shelf_slope", "shelf_intercept", "shelf_vs_fit_1V_pct", "shelf_vs_fit_2V_pct"]], on=["scope", "colour"]) .merge(runs.eid.reset_index(), on="scope").join(beacon_dark, on="scope")) fleet["pfd_1V"] = fleet.slope * produced(1.0) + fleet.intercept # the light you get asking for 1 V fleet["pfd_2V"] = fleet.slope * produced(2.0) + fleet.intercept fleet["saturated"] = fleet.apply(lambda r: int(d[(d.scope == r.scope) & (d.colour == r.colour)].saturated.sum()), axis=1) fleet = fleet.set_index(["scope", "channel"]).sort_index() fleet = fleet[["colour", "eid", "slope", "intercept", "slope_se", "pfd_1V", "pfd_2V", "r2", "resid_sd_pct", "lof_p", "readings_per_level", "hysteresis_max_pct", "repeat_pct", "beacon_pct", "beacon_dark_counts", "saturated", "shelf_slope", "shelf_intercept", "shelf_vs_fit_1V_pct", "shelf_vs_fit_2V_pct"]] os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True) fleet.to_csv(f"{OUT}/led_control_volt_vs_sample_intensity.csv") for eid, g in fleet.groupby("eid"): # one copy next to each run's data with open(os.path.join(exps.get_analysis_dir(eid), "led_control_volt_vs_sample_intensity.yaml"), "w") as fh: yaml.safe_dump({ch: {k: (v.item() if hasattr(v, "item") else v) for k, v in row.items()} for (_, ch), row in g.iterrows()}, fh) fleet.round(4)

    Acceptance¶

    This calibration writes to the scope, so it needs limits. The checks are: the light meter matches the constants (checked above), no saturated readings, each channel lights the colour it is named after, and the hysteresis, repeatability and fit residual stay within limits. The limits are not set yet; the values are in the results table.

    Persistent records¶

    This calibration writes 3 records to each scope: the shelves of its red, green and blue channels (~/red, ~/green, ~/blue). Each holds the fitted line (calib_slope, calib_intercept, calib_cov_matrix), the readings it was fitted on (calib_volts, calib_counts, calib_pfd), calib_dt, calib_sensor_gain, the light meter's report (calib_sensor), the constants used (calib_constants), and the run that produced it (calib_eid, calib_exp_dir).
